scenario.name: SANS DFIR & Microsoft Event Log — RDP Lateral Movement, Session Reconnection & BMC Bitmap Cache Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine an intruder sitting at one factory desk who opens a live remote video-and-keyboard booth into a restricted server room down the hall. Both the local desk diary and the distant room sign-in book automatically stamp matching connection receipts, while the local booth quietly saves hundreds of tiny square photo tiles of every window the intruder views, allowing forensic detectives to piece the intruder screen back together like a mosaic. In this scenario (T1021.001, SANS DFIR & Microsoft Event Log, RDP Lateral Movement, Session Reconnection & BMC Bitmap Cache Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry, then destination Server NLA Logon , RdpCoreTS 131, then client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Screen. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry, then Destination Server NLA Logon , RdpCoreTS 131, then Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Screen, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 11 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry & RDPClient EventID 1024 / 1102 on Source Host
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.001 - Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol)
stages.description: At the starting desk, the intruder types a target room address into the remote-viewing console. Even before the distant room answers, the desk personal address book and outgoing call ledger faithfully record the destination room and timestamp. When the attacker launches mstsc.exe on source host WKS-07 (10.10.4.19) to connect to SRV-APP02 (10.10.20.45), Windows records the target IP/hostname in NTUSER.DAT (Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45\UsernameHint) and logs EventID 1024 (RDP ClientActiveX is trying to connect) and EventID 1102 in Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RDPClient/Operational (logged in WinEvent Event 1024 with SourceHost=WKS-07.corp.local , 10.10.4.19, LogChannel=Microsoft-Windows-TerminalServices-RDPClient/Operational, EventID=1024 , Connection Attempt / 1102 , Server IP, RegistryMru=Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes mstsc.exe /v:10.10.20.45 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , mstsc.exe /v:10.10.20.45 via mstsc.exe, passing the exact arguments, target paths, and proto so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry & RDPClient EventID 1024 / 1102 on Source Host" , When the attacker launches mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Registry Artifact: NTUSER.DAT\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 (UsernameHint + CertHash) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Registry Artifact: NTUSER.DAT\Software\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Servers\10.10.20.45 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Outbound mstsc.exe Connection, MRU Registry & RDPClient EventID 1024 / 1102 on Source Host" , When the attacker launches mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ mstsc.exe /v:10.10.20.45 / ⇠#1 ACK 1024) from Node ① (#1 Pivot Host WKS-07 (mstsc.exe)) to Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 BMC Cache & Default.rdp Registry).

stages.title: Stage 2: Destination Server NLA Logon (EventID 4624 Type 10 / 7), RdpCoreTS 131 & LSM EventID 21 / 25
stages.subtitle: Lateral Movement (T1021.001 - Destination LSM EventID 21/24/25 & RdpCoreTS 131)
stages.description: When the connection lands in the restricted server room, three separate lobby ledgers wake up in sequence: the front network door logs the arriving IP address, the badge desk logs an interactive remote check-in, and the session desk notes whether the visitor started a fresh chair or slipped back into a disconnected one. On destination server SRV-APP02, Microsoft-Windows-RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational logs EventID 131 (Client IP:Port 10.10.4.19:54912), Security logs EventID 4624 (LogonType 10 RemoteInteractive or LogonType 7 when reconnecting to a locked session), and TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational logs EventID 21 (Session logon succeeded, Session ID 2) or EventID 25 (Session reconnection succeeded) (logged in WinEvent Event 21 with LogChannel=TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational, EventID=21 , Session Logon / 25 , Session Reconnect / 24 , Disconnect, SessionId=2, SourceNetworkAddress=10.10.4.19 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational EventID 131: ClientIP=10.10.4.19:54912 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational EventID 131: ClientIP=10.10.4.19:54912 via Syste so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Destination Server NLA Logon , EventID 4624 Type 10 / 7, RdpCoreTS 131 & LSM EventID 21 / 25" , On destination server SRV-APP02, Microsoft-Windows-RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational logs EventID 131 , Client IP:Port 10 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact Security EventID 4624: LogonType=10 (RemoteInteractive) IpAddress=10.10.4.19 runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Security EventID 4624: LogonType=10 , RemoteInteractive IpAddress=10.10.4.19 via System / Ru so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Destination Server NLA Logon , EventID 4624 Type 10 / 7, RdpCoreTS 131 & LSM EventID 21 / 25" , On destination server SRV-APP02, Microsoft-Windows-RemoteDesktopServices-RdpCoreTS/Operational logs EventID 131 , Client IP:Port 10 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ svchost.exe -k NetworkService -s TermService (Session 2 Logon from 10.10.4.19) / ⇠#2 ACK 21) from Node ② (#2 Core Identity & VLAN Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Internal VLAN Router (:3389)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 BMC Cache & Default.rdp Registry).

keySpecs.value: Correlate Security EventID 4624 (LogonType 10 and LogonType 7) with TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager/Operational EventIDs 21 and 25 so RDP session reconnections (which log as Type 7 instead of Type 10) are never missed.

stages.title: Stage 3: Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache (Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools) Visual Screen Reconstruction
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1021.001 - RDP Bitmap Cache Visual Reconstruction)
stages.description: To keep the remote video screen fast and smooth, the viewer console on the starting desk secretly stores hundreds of 64-by-64-pixel square picture tiles of every button, terminal line, and file folder shown on screen, leaving behind a visual mosaic that investigators can stitch back together even after the intruder clears every text log. During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc.exe on WKS-07 caches 64x64 pixel screen tiles inside %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (and bcache24.bmc). Using ANSSI bmc-tools and Rdpieces, DFIR analysts carve and reassemble the bitmap tiles from WKS-07 to visually reconstruct the exact GUI tools and commands the attacker ran on SRV-APP02 (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with ArtifactFile=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin, TileDimensions=64x64 Raw Bitmap Tiles, ForensicParser=ANSSI bmc-tools.py + Rdpieces, EvidentiaryValue=Visual reconstruction of attacker GUI actions on remote host so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b via python3, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ mstsc.exe writing 64x64 RDP bitmap tiles to Cache0000.bin / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Internal VLAN Router (:3389)) to Node ④ (#4 Target Server SRV-APP02 (TermService)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 BMC Cache & Default.rdp Registry).

steps.plainTitle: Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache (Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools) Visual Screen Reconstruction
steps.storyAnalogy: To keep the remote video screen fast and smooth, the viewer console on the starting desk secretly stores hundreds of 64-by-64-pixel square picture tiles of every button, terminal line, and file folder shown on screen, leaving behind a visual mosaic that investigators can stitch back together even after the intruder clears every text log.
steps.simpleExplanation: During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc.exe on WKS-07 caches 64x64 pixel screen tiles inside %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (and bcache24.bmc). Using ANSSI bmc-tools and Rdpieces, DFIR analysts carve and reassemble the bitmap tiles from WKS-07 to visually reconstruct the exact GUI tools and commands the attacker ran on SRV-APP02 (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with ArtifactFile=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin, TileDimensions=64x64 Raw Bitmap Tiles, ForensicParser=ANSSI bmc-tools.py + Rdpieces, EvidentiaryValue=Visual reconstruction of attacker GUI actions on remote host so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0000.bin (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , Artifact Path: C:\Users\admin_db\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Terminal Server Client\Cache\Cache0 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , python3 bmc-tools.py -s Cache0000.bin -d ./extracted_tiles -b via python3, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1021.001 during "Client-Side RDP Bitmap Cache , Cache0000.bin / bmc2-tools Visual Screen Reconstruction" , During the interactive session on SRV-APP02, mstsc while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
